title: Monthly assistance context coexists with housing pressure, and the pooled pattern reverses by resource context
source_unit: 2025 SIPP public-use person-month records for January–December 2024 reference period

observations.period: January–December 2024 reference period; month-t assistance to month-t+1 outcome pairs

denominator.unit: valid person-month pairs for the relevant weighted screen across assistance-exposed and unexposed cells

assistance_exposed_pairs.unit: unweighted valid person-month pairs with EOTHAS_MNYN=Yes

assistance_unexposed_pairs.unit: unweighted valid person-month pairs with EOTHAS_MNYN=No

observations.method: The screen used WPFINWGT from month t and 240 Census Fay–BRR replicate weights with perturbation factor 0.5. It retained person-month keys and compared month-t EOTHAS_MNYN, defined by the Census catalog as monthly other clothing or housing assistance, with next-month job-count movement, poverty-band movement, and reported inability to pay rent or mortgage.
observations.uncertainty: These are design-based intervals around weighted descriptive cells, not adjustment for selection into assistance and not causal confidence intervals. EOTHAS_MNYN combines clothing or housing assistance and does not identify a HUD program, amount, adequacy, application, or response route.
observations.subgroup: Persons with valid month-t assistance and month-t+1 outcome fields in the 2025 SIPP public-use file; household-level fields repeated on person records are not household prevalence estimates.
observations.counterinterpretation: Assistance may be targeted to people already under housing pressure, may protect some low-resource renters, or may be too small or mismatched for other groups. The later stratified audit shows the pooled housing-difficulty contrast changes direction across renter tenure and income-to-poverty contexts.

observations.period: January–December 2024 reference period; month-t renter and owner/buyer strata

denominator.unit: tenure-by-income-to-poverty context cells with exposed and unexposed comparisons

renter_below_2x_poverty_direction.value: Exposed renters below 2× poverty had lower reported next-month difficulty than unexposed renters in both below-1× and 1–2× strata

renter_above_2x_poverty_direction.value: The direction reversed in the 2–4× and 4×+ renter strata, with exposed difficulty estimates above unexposed estimates

owner_exposed_precision.value: Exposed owner/buyer cells were small and had wide intervals; the 4×+ zero estimate is not evidence of no risk

observations.method: The pooled screen was crossed by month-t tenure context and income-to-poverty band before comparing the same next-month reported housing-difficulty outcome, retaining Fay–BRR uncertainty.
observations.uncertainty: ETENURE is interview-period context rather than a monthly move transition. The exposed owner cells are sparse and imprecise, and the assistance field combines clothing and housing routes.
observations.subgroup: Renter and owner/buyer persons grouped by month-t income-to-poverty band.
observations.counterinterpretation: The reversal may reflect selection, protection, different housing-cost structures, assistance mismatch, or composition rather than a causal effect of assistance.

related_sources.claim: Official Census SIPP data page documents the 2025 public-use release.
Official Census variable catalog supplies field definitions and timing context.

boundary: This record adds a same-person descriptive bridge from monthly other assistance context to next-month housing difficulty, work, and resource movement, plus a stratified counterexample. It does not establish a causal assistance effect, HUD program receipt, benefit adequacy, alternatives, landlord or agency response, arrears, eviction, homelessness, verified recovery, trust, or political action.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Primary and replicate archive hashes are preserved in the local SIPP timing and weighted-screen machine-readable summaries; the large raw respondent archive remains outside Git.
